facts.statement: The genus Abavornis is tentatively assigned to the Enantiornithes based on a single broken coracoid fossil that resembles typical members of that group.
facts.quote: It was probably a member of the Enantiornithes, but as it is only known from a single broken coracoid (TsNIGRI 56/11915), which, however, looks typically enantiornithine, that assignment is tentative.

facts.statement: The type fossil of Abavornis was found in the Bissekty Formation in the Kyzylkum region of Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: The fossil is from Late Cretaceous Bissekty Formation (Turonian, 92 MYA) in the Kyzylkum, Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: A second partial coracoid fossil, designated Abavornis sp., is similar to the type specimen and may belong to the same species, potentially revealing damaged features of the holotype.
facts.quote: Another partial coracoid (PO 4605) is very similar and is referred to as Abavornis sp.; it might belong to A. bonaparti and if so show some features which are damaged in the holotype.

facts.statement: Abavornis is classified within the subclass Enantiornithes.
The genus Abavornis belongs to the parent group Alexornithidae.
Abavornis lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus Abavornis is A. bonaparti.
The species name bonaparti honors the Argentine paleontologist José Bonaparte.
facts.quote: (named in honor of the Argentine paleontologist José Bonaparte)
